title: Detected routes covered four of 83 polysynaptic calls in selected Allen human temporal-cortex pairs
abstract: We tested whether measured chemical connections among recorded cells provide routes for manually detected polysynaptic responses in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 small. We selected pairs with no detected direct chemical connection. In human temporal cortex, four of 83 positive calls had a measured two-step route; longer routes did not increase coverage. Only one call had a two-step route with matching measured signs. A passed-response-fit rule retained four routes in 81 calls. Exact within-recording label tests gave no clear route enrichment (upper-tail p=0.1003); source or class, distance, and test-spike controls increased p. Mouse visual cortex had only two positive calls, neither with a measured route, and no conditional test variation. The result limits explanations based on the sparse observed graphs. It does not exclude unrecorded relays, missed connections, electrical paths, or call errors. Code, aggregate results, and a figure are included. External raw data and record-level outputs remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Measured chemical routes cover few selected human temporal-cortex polysynaptic calls. Exact null means increase after cell and detection controls. These are sparse physiological graphs, not complete anatomical circuits.
